svg.title: Modbus register addressing: value width and word order
svg.desc: Four 16-bit holding registers at PDU addresses 100 to 103 (vendor numbering 40101 to 40104). INT16 and UINT16 occupy register 100 only; INT32, UINT32 and FLOAT32 occupy 100 and 101; FLOAT64 occupies 100 to 103 — all configured as Identifier HoldingRegister:100, so the Datatype alone decides how many registers a value covers. The lower panel reads one INT32 from the same two registers, where HoldingRegister:100 holds 10 (0x000A) and HoldingRegister:101 holds 0 (0x0000). With WordOrder HighWordFirst, register 100 is the high word and register 101 the low word, assembling the 32 bits 0000 0000 0000 1010 0000 0000 0000 0000, that is 10 times 65536 plus 0, giving 655360 (0x000A0000). With WordOrder LowWordFirst the roles swap: register 101 becomes the high word and register 100 the low word, assembling 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 1010, that is 0 times 65536 plus 10, giving 10 (0x0000000A). A wrong WordOrder therefore returns a plausible-looking but badly wrong number rather than an error.
svg.text: The PDU address goes in Identifier. The Datatype decides how many 16-bit registers the value covers.
Do not configure a second stream on an address a wider value already covers.
Datatype: INT32 at Identifier: HoldingRegister:100 — the same two registers, two WordOrder settings.
